Lockheed Martin's (NYSE: LMT) Record $292 Billion Backlog And Valuation Discount Make A Compelling Investment Case
sum: A book-to-bill ratio of 4.0 in the third quarter of 2026 signals that Lockheed Martin (NYSE: LMT) is pulling in new orders at a pace that far outstrips its current revenue base.
That demand surge pushed the company’s backlog to a record $292 billion as of September 27, 2026, up sharply from $230 billion just one quarter earlier.
Despite that extraordinary momentum, LMT shares trade at a forward 12-month price-to-sales ratio of just 1.56X, a meaningful discount to the aerospace-defense industry average of 2.16X.
That valuation gap has emerged even as the stock has climbed 12% over the past six months, a period during which the broader Zacks Aerospace-Defense industry fell 8.8%.

The outperformance reflects a wave of major contract awards, including a seven-year PAC-3 missile defense agreement valued at up to $58.6 billion and a separate seven-year THAAD deal worth $35 billion.

Allied demand for advanced air and missile defense systems also drove a $439 million ATACMS production contract tied to Taiwan’s HIMARS launchers and an $800 million award for Australia’s AIR6500 battle management program.
On October 26, 2026, Lockheed completed its $3.45 billion acquisition of Ultra Maritime, a specialist in undersea and anti-submarine warfare technologies serving allied naval forces globally.

Is Lockheed Martin Stock Priced Right Against Its Peers?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Lockheed Martin (LMT) keeps more of its sales as operating profit than four of its five aerospace and defense peers, tying the fifth, RTX. The stock returned 25.1% from November 3, 2025 to November 4, 2026, the best in the group. Yet on price against earnings, Lockheed ranks only fourth of the five companies with a usable P/E. If not the margin, what are investors paying for in this group?

Investors in this group appear to pay for sales growth more than for margin. On growth, Lockheed also ranks fourth of six companies. RTX shows the contrast most sharply. Over their latest four quarters, both companies kept 11.8% of sales as operating profit, yet investors pay 31.9 times earnings for RTX against 21.1 for Lockheed. One difference between the two is sales growth: RTX grew revenue 11.6% over that period, against 7.9% for Lockheed.

Most of the rest of the group fits the same pattern. General Dynamics grows faster than Lockheed and trades at a slightly higher P/E, while Northrop Grumman grows slower and trades lower. Only L3Harris is priced above Lockheed with slower growth.

In 2025, Lockheed's missiles business, Missiles and Fire Control, grew sales 13.6% to $15.3 billion. Its largest business, Aeronautics, which makes the F-35 jet, grew more slowly, up 5.7% to $30.6 billion.

Lockheed's growth over the past four quarters includes a first quarter of fiscal 2026 in which sales barely rose from a year earlier. Sales then grew 10.5% in the second quarter and 11.3% in the third. Management said every segment grew in the third quarter, and sales at Missiles and Fire Control rose 24%.

Lockheed also ended the third quarter with a record $292 billion backlog, the orders it has yet to turn into sales. That is up $113 billion from a year earlier. The largest addition in the quarter was a seven-year contract for PAC-3 interceptors.

Defense Stocks Fall After Democrats Win Congress, Putting 2027 Budget in Focus
sum: Defense stocks fell Wednesday after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress, as investors assessed whether the new majority would challenge President Donald Trump’s defense spending priorities.

Lockheed Martin shares fell 3.6% in Wednesday’s session. L3Harris lost more than 2%, while RTX Corporation and Northrop Grumman each dropped more than 3%. The moves followed Tuesday’s midterm results and drew attention to federal budget choices that shape demand for defense contractors’ products and services.

Each company has significant government exposure. About 70% of Lockheed Martin’s sales come from the U.S. government, while U.S. government sales made up 75% of L3Harris’ fiscal 2025 revenue. L3Harris’ figure includes sales through prime contractors, including foreign military sales. RTX and Northrop Grumman also generate significant sales through U.S. government contracts.

That reliance leaves the companies exposed to congressional review of the administration’s spending agenda. Wednesday’s market reaction reflected concern that a Democratic majority could challenge President Trump’s priorities, adding uncertainty for contractors that depend on public funding.

Wolfe Research analyst Myles Walton called the Democratic sweep a “headline negative” for defense shares, but said the first reaction could be “potentially short-lived.” Walton pointed to the 2006 midterms, when Republicans held the White House and Democrats captured both chambers of Congress.

Defense shares initially fell about 2% after that election, then recovered while military budgets continued rising. Democrats later backed increased funding for U.S. operations in Iraq. The episode shows why an election result alone does not settle the direction of defense spending.

The historical comparison comes as the current backdrop includes the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine war. A roughly 20% decline from the sector’s summer peak had already put aerospace and defense shares under pressure, a pullback discussed in an earlier analysis of a possible tactical bottom for the sector.

AI data center stocks dip, renewables surge after Democrat sweep in US midterm elections
sum: Nov 4 (Reuters) – Data center stocks slipped in premarket trading on Wednesday, while clean-energy shares surged after Democrats won both the Senate and the House, raising prospects of tougher oversight of the AI boom alongside fresh backing for renewables.
The Democrats scored sweeping victories in Republican strongholds such as Kansas for the first time in generations.
Texas and Georgia, which are key states for data centers given their ability to host large-scale facilities, also elected Democratic candidates.
The results will usher in a divided government in Washington, following two years in which the Republican-controlled Congress rarely exercised its power to rein in President Donald Trump.
Market reaction spanned sectors including AI-linked stocks, renewables, healthcare companies and prison operators.
Data center operators lost ground, with Core Scientific down 2.8% and Iren down 1.4%. Applied Digital and CoreWeave were marginally lower.

The data center boom triggered public backlash this year, stoking concerns that tighter Democratic oversight could curb spending momentum at a time when investors are becoming wary of mounting AI outlays yet to deliver strong financial returns.

sum: Shares of Lockheed Martin LMT have gained 9.6% following the defense giant’s better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 22. The rally was driven by revenue and earnings beats, along with a record backlog count, which reached an all-time high of $292 billion.

The backlog was boosted by a massive $52.5 billion multi-year award for PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement interceptors, reflecting surging global demand for missile defense systems. The company’s raised full-year forecast likely further bolstered investor sentiment, contributing to the stock’s climb.

However, the company’s cash flow situation presented a nuanced picture. Lockheed generated $3 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, representing a 9% decline from the prior-year period’s level. As the company remains in negotiations with the U.S. government over production contracts for F-35 Lots 20 and higher, Lockheed’s future cash flow may suffer a decline if additional funding is not received.
Against this backdrop, investors might want to consider exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with substantial exposure to Lockheed Martin as an alternative to investing directly in the stock.

These ETFs will offer an opportunity to benefit from a potential rally in LMT stock, driven by geopolitical tensions and a seemingly insatiable demand for munitions and air defense, while avoiding the idiosyncratic risk and sharp volatility associated with a single-stock position.

Before exploring the best ETF options for gaining exposure to Lockheed Martin, let us take a closer look at the company’s third-quarter performance across key operational metrics and assess how the market, particularly credit rating agencies, responded to its results.

The company’s third-quarter earnings of $7.97 beat the Zacks consensus estimate by 6.4%, while its sales of $20.7 billion topped the consensus mark by 1.4%. On a year-over-year basis, both revenues and earnings recorded double-digit growth.

sum: Two companies report earnings on the same morning, but retirement investors only have room for one. Before the opening bell on July 23, the gap between these two stocks tells a story worth understanding.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Both American Airlines (NASDAQ:AAL | AAL Price Prediction) and Lockheed Martin (NYSE:LMT) report Q2 2026 results before the open on Thursday, July 23, 2026. Retirement-focused investors face one plain question: which one deserves the portfolio slot right now? One is a $10.1 billion airline still climbing out of losses, while the other is a defense prime with a record backlog and 23 consecutive years of dividend increases. Here is what the data says heading into the same-session double-header.

Lockheed Martin’s most recent quarter delivered diluted EPS of $6.44, a miss of 3.9% versus the $6.70 estimate, on revenue of $18.02 billion (+0.32% year over year). That followed FY 2025 diluted EPS of $21.49 on revenue of $75.05 billion (+5.64%), with free cash flow of $6.91 billion (+30.66%). Management reaffirmed FY 2026 diluted EPS guidance of $29.35 to $30.25 and free cash flow of $6.5 billion to $6.8 billion.

American Airlines topped expectations last quarter: Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of −$0.40 versus a −$0.46 estimate (+13.04%) on record revenue of $13.91 billion (+10.84% year over year). But the full-year picture is far wider: FY 2026 adjusted EPS guidance runs from −$0.40 to $1.10, with more than $4 billion in incremental fuel expense weighing on results. FY 2025 delivered adjusted EPS of just $0.36 and free cash flow of −$83 million.
Winner: Lockheed Martin. A $29 to $30 EPS band paired with about 25% segment operating profit growth beats a range that spans a loss to a slim profit.

Lockheed Martin (LMT) is reportedly leading the race to acquire Ultra Maritime, owned by private equity firm Advent International, in a deal that could value the naval defense business at about $3.5 billion.
Shares of Lockheed Martin (LMT) rose 4.62% on Thursday before edging lower in after-hours trading. At the time of writing, the LMT stock was down 0.3%.

Lockheed Martin has emerged as the frontrunner to acquire Ultra Maritime, a division of Advent's Cobham Ultra business that specializes in anti-submarine warfare and undersea defense technologies, reported the Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter.

Talks are ongoing, and a deal could be announced as early as next week, according to the report. It added that several other bidders remain interested in Ultra Maritime as part of a competitive auction process.
